Calculate Pair Correlation Within Distance Bands Around Tumor Polygons

calculate_pcf_by_band.Rd

Splits the outside-tumor region into bands that follow the tumor contour (band 1 = `band_breaks[1]` to `band_breaks[2]` from the tumor boundary, and so on) and computes the cross pair correlation function g(r) for every cell-type pair separately in each band. This shows whether co-localization of two cell types changes with distance from the tumor.

Usage

calculate_pcf_by_band(
  seurat_obj,
  polygons,
  celltype_col,
  band_width = 25,
  max_distance = NULL,
  band_breaks = NULL,
  approach = c("restricted", "anchored"),
  distance = 20,
  null_model = c("label_shuffle", "csr", "none"),
  nsim = 99,
  bw = 10,
  min_cells = 10,
  fov_name = "fov",
  include_self_pairs = TRUE,
  ordered_pairs = NULL,
  window_obj = NULL,
  tissue_window = c("concave", "convex", "bbox"),
  p_adjust_method = "BH",
  show_progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

seurat_obj

Seurat object with spatial coordinates.

polygons

sf polygon object representing tumor regions.

celltype_col

Metadata column containing cell type labels.

band_width

Band width in coordinate units (microns). Ignored when `band_breaks` is supplied.

max_distance

Outer edge of the last band. `NULL` covers all outside cells (rounded up to a whole band). Ignored when `band_breaks` is supplied.

band_breaks

Optional increasing numeric vector of band edges, e.g. `c(0, 25, 50, 100, 200)`. Overrides `band_width` and `max_distance`. Cells closer than the first or at least the last break are in no band.

approach

`"restricted"` or `"anchored"`. See Details.

distance

Cell-to-cell distance(s) r at which g is reported. One value or a vector.

null_model

`"label_shuffle"`, `"csr"`, or `"none"`. See Details.

nsim

Number of simulations for the null model.

bw

Kernel bandwidth passed to `spatstat.explore::pcfmulti()`. `NULL` uses the `spatstat` default.

min_cells

Minimum cells of a type needed to compute g for it: per band for both types with `"restricted"`; per band for the anchor type and over the whole outside region for the neighbor type with `"anchored"`. Types with fewer than `min_cells` outside cells overall are dropped entirely.

fov_name

Field of view/image name passed to `Seurat::GetTissueCoordinates`.

include_self_pairs

Logical; include same-type pairs.

ordered_pairs

Logical; compute both A-B and B-A. `NULL` (default) uses `TRUE` for `"anchored"` and `FALSE` for `"restricted"`.

window_obj

Optional `spatstat.geom::owin` tissue window; tumor polygons are subtracted from it.

tissue_window

Tissue outline used when `window_obj` is `NULL`: `"concave"`, `"convex"`, or `"bbox"`. See [build_outside_window()].

p_adjust_method

Method passed to [stats::p.adjust()].

show_progress

Logical; show a text progress bar.

Value

Data frame with one row per band, pair and distance: `band`, `band_inner`, `band_outer`, `band_label`, `type1`, `type2`, `distance`, `g_value`, `n_type1`, `n_type2` (cells used: in the band, or for the anchored neighbor type, in the whole outside region), and when a null model is used `null_mean`, `null_lo`, `null_hi` (2.5 quantiles), `p_value`, `p_adj`. Attributes: `approach`, `null_model`, `nsim`, `bw`, `band_breaks`, `ordered_pairs`, and `bands` (an sf object of band polygons for plotting).

Details

Band membership uses each cell's exact distance to the nearest tumor polygon (the same definition as the `"band_permutation"` null in [plot_pcf_outside_pair_envelopes()]). Band shapes follow the irregular tumor outline and are clipped to the tissue window.

Two approaches are available: * `"restricted"`: each band is its own observation window and only cells in that band are used, for both cell types. g(r) answers "within this band, are type-2 cells concentrated around type-1 cells, relative to the band's own cell mix?". Bands are thin, so circles of radius r larger than the band width mostly fall outside the band and estimates become noisy; keep `distance` at or below roughly the band width. * `"anchored"`: type-1 ("anchor") cells come from the band; type-2 ("neighbor") cells can be anywhere outside the tumor, and the window is the whole outside-tumor region. g(r) answers "around type-1 cells located in this band, how dense are type-2 cells at distance r, relative to type-2 density over the whole outside region?". Not symmetric in the two types, so ordered pairs are used by default. Larger `distance` values are usable, but with `null_model = "csr"` the tumor gradient is not accounted for (see below).

Null models (Monte Carlo, `nsim` simulations): * `"label_shuffle"`: cell positions are kept and cell-type labels are randomly permuted. With `"restricted"`, labels are permuted among cells in the band. With `"anchored"`, labels are permuted within every band (cells beyond the last band form their own group), so each band keeps its cell-type composition and the distance-to-tumor gradient is preserved. Tests co-localization beyond what the band's composition and cell layout explain. * `"csr"`: complete spatial randomness. With `"restricted"`, every cell in the band is moved to a uniformly random position within the band, keeping its type. With `"anchored"`, anchor cells keep their real positions and every other outside-tumor cell is moved to a uniformly random position in the outside window. CSR also flags ordinary clumping of cells, and in `"anchored"` mode it also flags any distance-to-tumor gradient. * `"none"`: observed g only.

The p-value is a two-sided Monte Carlo test at each `distance`: `(1 + k) / (nsim_ok + 1)`, where `k` is the number of simulations with `abs(g_sim - null_mean) >= abs(g_obs - null_mean)` and `nsim_ok` is the number of simulations giving a finite g. `p_adj` adjusts these across all rows of the result (all bands, pairs and distances) with `p_adjust_method`.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- calculate_pcf_by_band(seurat_obj, auto_polygons, celltype_col = "cellType",
                             band_width = 50, max_distance = 200,
                             approach = "restricted", distance = 20,
                             null_model = "label_shuffle", nsim = 99)
plot_pcf_band_heatmap(res)
plot_pcf_band_profile(res)
} # }
